mainTopic: Voluntary offerings on the festivals: the תודה, בל תאחר, and whether a תודה can count as חגיגה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier discussion: everyone agrees that נדרים ונדבות are not brought on יום טוב itself. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא with three views about bringing a תודה on the festivals: the תנא קמא, רבי שמעון, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. It explains that the ban on a תודה 'on פסח' really refers to ערב פסח, because we do not bring קדשים into a situation likely to disqualify them. The תנא קמא allows a תודה only on חול המועד of סוכות. When רבי זירא objects to reading רבי שמעון as forbidding offerings on חול המועד, אביי explains that the real argument is about when a person violates בל תאחר: any three רגלים, or only three in their order. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is shown to allow a תודה even on the יום טוב of סוכות. He names סוכות because of his own view that סוכות is the festival that sets the deadline. Finally, the גמרא explains that a תודה counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה, even if the person stipulated otherwise. It then begins a parallel question that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: vow and gift offerings are not brought on the Festival day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion. Whatever the argument about obligatory festival offerings, everyone agrees that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, vow-offerings and gift-offerings: everyone agrees they are not sacrificed on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier argument by stating where everyone agrees. Voluntary offerings are never brought on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל was limited to the festival's own required offerings, like the עולת ראייה. נדרים ונדבות are not part of the festival's obligation, so no one allows them on יום טוב. They have to wait for a weekday, such as חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow-offerings: a person says 'I take upon myself to bring an offering'
Gift-offerings: a person sets aside a specific animal as an offering
Everyone agrees
The Festival day itself, not חול המועד

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב itself, only offerings connected to the festival may be brought. נדרים ונדבות are not allowed, according to everyone.

phrases.english: However, vow-offerings and gift-offerings
all agree
they are not sacrificed on the Festival day.
phrases.notes: Continues the statement of עולא and רב אדא בר אהבה from the earlier part of the דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over earlier about which offerings may be brought on יום טוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נדרים ונדבות are not brought on יום טוב according to all opinions.

steps.title: A parallel argument between תנאים about the thanks-offering on the festivals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the same kind of argument appears elsewhere among תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about bringing a תודה on פסח, שבועות, and סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים are like those תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: A תודה may not be brought on פסח, because of the חמץ that comes with it. It may not be brought on שבועות either, because it is יום טוב. But a person may bring his תודה on סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another ברייתא contains a similar argument between תנאים. This step quotes the first opinion in that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה comes with forty loaves, ten of which are חמץ, so it cannot be brought on פסח. On שבועות it is not allowed because שבועות is a one-day יום טוב, and a voluntary offering cannot be brought on יום טוב. סוכות is allowed because it has days of חול המועד when voluntary offerings may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים
As it is taught in a ברייתא
Thanks-offering, which is brought with forty loaves, including ten of חמץ
Leavened bread, forbidden on פסח
The name the משנה and ברייתא use for שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תודה is banned on שבועות because of its חמץ. חמץ is allowed on שבועות. The only problem there is that it is יום טוב, and a voluntary offering cannot be brought on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And these Tannaim are like those Tannaim,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One may not bring a thanks-offering on the festival of Matzot,
because of the leavened bread that comes with it.
And not on Shavuot
because it is a Festival day.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵבִיא אָדָם תּוֹדָתוֹ בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: But a person may bring his thanks-offering on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel argument from another ברייתא, connected to the topic of voluntary offerings on festivals.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים argue about which offerings may be brought on the festivals
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about bringing a תודה on פסח, שבועות, and סוכות

steps.title: רבי שמעון: all three festivals follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק that groups the three festivals together: any offering that can come on פסח can come on the others, and any offering that cannot come on פסח cannot come on the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The פסוק says 'On the festival of מצות, on the festival of שבועות, and on the festival of סוכות.' Whatever comes on פסח comes on שבועות and סוכות. Whatever does not come on פסח does not come on שבועות and סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the ברייתא. רבי שמעון uses the פסוק to put all three festivals under one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק lists the three festivals together, רבי שמעון compares them to each other. A תודה cannot come on פסח because of its חמץ. So, by this comparison, it cannot come on סוכות either. This disagrees with the תנא קמא, who allowed a תודה on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: But the פסוק says, used to bring proof from a verse
The festival of מצות, which is פסח
The festival of שבועות
The festival of סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
But it says:
"On the festival of Matzot, on the festival of Shavuot, and on the festival of Sukkot"
Anything that comes on the festival of Matzot
comes on Shavuot and on Sukkot,
and anything that does not come on the festival of Matzot

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ בָּא בְּחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: does not come on Shavuot or on Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about bringing a תודה on סוכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three festivals share one rule. Since a תודה cannot come on פסח, it cannot come on שבועות or סוכות either.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: the thanks-offering counts for rejoicing, not for the festival offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows a תודה on סוכות. Eating it fulfills the obligation of שמחה, but it does not count as the חגיגה offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: A person may bring his תודה on סוכות. With it he fulfills his obligation of שמחה, but he does not fulfill his obligation of חגיגה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third opinion in the ברייתא. It allows a תודה on סוכות and explains which festival obligation it fulfills.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמחה on the festival is fulfilled by eating the meat of שלמים, and any such meat works, including a תודה. The חגיגה is a specific required festival offering, so an offering already owed for another reason cannot count for it. The גמרא will later show (step 18) that he means even the יום טוב of סוכות itself, which the תנא קמא forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfills his obligation
The מצוה to rejoice on the festival by eating meat of שלמים
The required שלמים offering brought on the festival

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has three views. תנא קמא: a תודה may be brought on סוכות. רבי שמעון: links all three festivals to the rule of פסח. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: it may be brought on סוכות, and it counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה. The גמרא explains each view more precisely later in the breakdown.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
A person may bring his thanks-offering on Sukkot,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה,
phrases.english: and fulfills with it his obligation of rejoicing,
but does not fulfill with it the Festival-offering obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view, allowing a תודה on סוכות and adding which obligation it fulfills. The גמרא later shows he differs from the תנא קמא by allowing it even on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה on סוכות fulfills שמחה but not חגיגה.

steps.title: Why would the ברייתא need to tell us there is no thanks-offering on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא and asks: isn't it obvious that an offering that includes חמץ cannot be brought on פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'A תודה may not be brought on פסח because of the חמץ that comes with it.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to analyze the ברייתא. It challenges the first line as saying something too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows חמץ is forbidden on פסח. A ברייתא should not waste words on something so plain. So the line must be teaching something new, and the next step explains what.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said, used to quote a line from a source and analyze it
It is obvious! A challenge that the statement teaches nothing new

phrases.english: The Master said:
One may not bring a thanks-offering on the festival of Matzot
because of the leavened bread that comes with it.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אֵין מְבִיאִין תּוֹדָה בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת מִפְּנֵי חָמֵץ שֶׁבָּהּ פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first line of the ברייתא quoted in step 2 to examine it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תודה may not be brought on פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is obvious that an offering containing חמץ cannot be brought on פסח, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the day before פסח, the fourteenth of ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק (or רב שמואל בר אבא) answers that the ברייתא is talking about ערב פסח. It teaches that we do not bring קדשים into a situation that makes them more likely to become disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק said, and some say it was רב שמואל בר אבא: Here we are dealing with the fourteenth of ניסן. This תנא holds that we do not bring קדשים into a situation that makes them more likely to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. The ברייתא is really talking about ערב פסח, when a new and less obvious rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה normally may be eaten for a day and the following night. On ערב פסח, though, its חמץ loaves must be finished by midday, so much of the eating time is lost and leftovers become נותר. Bringing it then knowingly sets it up to be disqualified, and that is forbidden. This is the new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it was said by someone else
Here we are dealing with a specific case
The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח
We do not bring holy offerings into a situation that makes them likely to become disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: On ערב פסח, חמץ is still allowed until midday. The problem is not eating חמץ on פסח. The problem is that the time to eat the offering is cut short, which puts it at risk of becoming נותר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול appears across ש״ס. It means a person may not take an action that knowingly shortens the time allowed for eating an offering.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'obvious' line in the ברייתא is about ערב פסח. It teaches the rule against bringing קדשים into a situation likely to disqualify them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rav Adda, son of Rav Yitzchak, said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Shmuel bar Abba:
Here we are dealing with the fourteenth of Nisan,
and this Tanna holds:
one may not bring consecrated offerings into a situation of likely disqualification.
phrases.notes: The time to eat the תודה is shortened because the חמץ must be finished before midday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by moving the ברייתא's case to ערב פסח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about פסח itself, which would make it obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about the fourteenth of ניסן. It teaches that we do not bring קדשים into a situation likely to disqualify them.

steps.title: No thanks-offering on שבועות because it is a festival day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a תודה may not be brought on עצרת (שבועות) because it is a יום טוב. The גמרא explains that this תנא holds נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And not on עצרת, because it is a יום טוב." The גמרא explains: this תנא holds that vowed and donated offerings are not brought on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next line of the ברייתא and explains the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח the problem with a תודה was חמץ. שבועות has no חמץ problem, so a different reason is needed. That reason is that this תנא holds voluntary offerings (נדרים ונדבות) may not be brought on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for שבועות
Voluntary offerings: one a person vowed to bring (נדר) and one he donated (נדבה)
"He holds": introduces the opinion behind a ruling

phrases.english: And not on Atzeret (Shavuot),
because it is a Festival day.
He holds: vow-offerings and gift-offerings
are not sacrificed on a Festival day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the ברייתא after the first line about פסח was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, נדרים ונדבות, including a תודה, are not brought on יום טוב itself.

steps.title: When exactly may a thanks-offering be brought on סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a person may bring his תודה on סוכות. The גמרא asks: at what point during סוכות?
steps.simpleTranslation: "But a person may bring his תודה on סוכות." When?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next line of the ברייתא and asks which days of סוכות it means. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכות has two kinds of days: יום טוב itself and חול המועד. The ברייתא did not say which one, so the גמרא wants the case defined exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: "When?": asks for the exact time or case
A thanks-offering, brought together with loaves, some of them חמץ

phrases.english: However, a person may bring his thanks-offering
on the festival of Sukkot.
When?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the ברייתא and asks for its exact time frame.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'on סוכות' mean on יום טוב itself or on חול המועד?

steps.title: It cannot mean the festival day itself
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא meant יום טוב itself, it would contradict its own earlier line that forbids a תודה on שבועות because it is a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say on יום טוב itself, didn't you just say: "And not on עצרת, because it is a יום טוב"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible answer and shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already explained that a תודה is not brought on שבועות because it is a יום טוב. That reason applies equally to the יום טוב of סוכות, so the ברייתא cannot be allowing a תודה on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say": introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to reject
"But didn't you say": points to a contradiction with an earlier statement
The festival day itself, as opposed to the in-between days

phrases.english: If we say on the Festival day itself,
but didn't you say:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בָּעֲצֶרֶת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: "And not on Shavuot, because it is a Festival day"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'on סוכות' as meaning the יום טוב day itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: the ברייתא already forbade a תודה on שבועות because it is a יום טוב, and the same reason applies to the יום טוב of סוכות.

steps.title: It means the intermediate days of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean that a תודה may be brought on חול המועד of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only answer left: the ברייתא is talking about חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חול המועד is not a full יום טוב, so the rule against נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב does not apply. Unlike פסח, סוכות has no חמץ problem, so a תודה is fine on its in-between days.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate, less holy days of the festival (חול המועד)
"Rather": introduces the correct reading after rejecting another

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא: no תודה on פסח (חמץ), no תודה on יום טוב itself (no נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב), but a תודה is allowed on חול המועד of סוכות.

phrases.english: Rather, on the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of step 9 by choosing the other possibility.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (narrowing the time frame)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might have meant the יום טוב of סוכות itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means חול המועד of סוכות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule linking all three festivals, read again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי שמעון's words from the ברייתא: whatever can come on פסח can come on שבועות and סוכות, and whatever cannot come on פסח cannot come on them. This seems to forbid a תודה even on חול המועד of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the פסוק says "on חג המצות, on חג השבועות, and on חג הסוכות." Anything that comes on חג המצות comes on שבועות and סוכות, and anything that does not come on חג המצות does not come on שבועות or סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reads רבי שמעון's part of the ברייתא in order to examine what it means. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה cannot come at all during פסח, even on חול המועד, because of its חמץ loaves. So רבי שמעון's rule seems to mean a תודה cannot come on any day of סוכות either, even חול המועד. That is the opposite of what the תנא קמא just allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: "Behold, it says": introduces a פסוק as proof
The festival of מצות, which is פסח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. The גמרא already quoted it in step 3. It is quoted again here so that the גמרא can now challenge what it seems to say about חול המועד.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: But it says,
"On the festival of Matzot, and on the festival of Shavuot,
and on the festival of Sukkot,"
anything that comes on the festival of Matzot
comes on the festival of Shavuot and on the festival of Sukkot,
and anything that does not come on the festival of Matzot

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ בָּא בְּחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: does not come on the festival of Shavuot or on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the תנא קמא, the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's part of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the פסוק that groups the festivals together, an offering that cannot come on פסח (like a תודה) cannot come on שבועות or סוכות. Read simply, this includes even חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי זירא: if chopping wood is allowed, surely offerings are
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: on חול המועד we may even chop wood, so how could voluntary offerings be forbidden then?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged it: Now, if we may even chop wood on חול המועד, is there any question about נדרים ונדבות?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the reading that רבי שמעון forbids a תודה on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary work like chopping wood is allowed on חול המועד for festival needs. Bringing a holy offering is surely no worse, so forbidding נדרים ונדבות on חול המועד makes no sense. The argument works from the less obvious case to the more obvious one.

keyTerms.meaning: "He challenged it": a strong objection by an אמורא
"Now": opens a 'this is already allowed, so surely that is' argument
"We chop (wood)": an ordinary task allowed on חול המועד
"Is it even a question?": the answer is obvious

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to it:
Now, if we may even chop wood (on the intermediate days),
is it even a question about vow-offerings and gift-offerings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the simple reading of רבי שמעון's rule from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding that רבי שמעון forbids a תודה on חול המועד of סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: even chopping wood is allowed on חול המועד, so bringing offerings must certainly be allowed.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is about the prohibition of delaying
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that everyone agrees offerings may be brought on חול המועד. The argument is actually about when a person becomes liable for בל תאחר, the prohibition against delaying a promised offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: about bringing the offering, everyone agrees it is permitted. Where they argue is about when a person becomes liable for בל תאחר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא by moving the argument to a different topic. It is not about what may be offered on the festivals but about the deadline for paying a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is now no argument about bringing the offering: both opinions allow it on חול המועד. רבי שמעון's festival grouping is really about counting the festivals that must pass before a person violates בל תאחר. The גמרא will explain this further next.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually offering a קרבן on the מזבח
"Everyone": all opinions agree
The prohibition against delaying a vowed or pledged offering (דברים כג:כב)
"To become liable for it": the point at which a person violates the prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, both תנאים allow a תודה on חול המועד. רבי שמעון's grouping of the three festivals is about the deadline of בל תאחר, not about which offerings may be brought.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the whole argument from the laws of the festival to the laws of vows. It sets up the next part of the sugya about how many festivals must pass before a person violates בל תאחר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Regarding the sacrificing, everyone
does not disagree that it is permitted.
Where they disagree
is about when one becomes liable for "You shall not delay."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּהַקְרָבָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי זירא's challenge by redefining what the argument is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the topic of the dispute (from permission to offer, to liability for delay)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון forbids bringing a תודה on חול המועד of סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone allows bringing it on חול המועד. רבי שמעון's festival rule concerns when a person becomes liable for בל תאחר.

steps.title: The first opinion: the three festivals count in any order
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that any three רגלים passing makes a person liable for בל תאחר, even if they do not come in the Torah's order.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that the Torah said 'three festivals,' and they count even if they are not in their order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's answer by explaining the first side of the argument. According to the תנא קמא, any three רגלים in a row count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the count can start with סוכות. A תודה cannot be brought on פסח because it comes with חמץ loaves. It also cannot be brought on שבועות, which has only one day, a יום טוב, and no חול המועד. So if a person skips סוכות, he will reach his deadline with no festival chance to bring it. That is why the תנא קמא tells him to bring it on חול המועד of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
Not in their (Torah) order

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
The Merciful One said 'three festivals',
even if they are not in their order.
phrases.notes: Any three festivals in a row count toward the deadline.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the בל תאחר argument that אביי introduced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא counts any three רגלים, so a person should bring his תודה on סוכות to avoid missing the deadline.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the festivals must pass in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that בל תאחר applies only when the three רגלים pass in the תורה's order.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds: in their order, yes; not in their order, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of אביי's explanation: רבי שמעון counts the festivals only in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the count runs פסח, שבועות, סוכות, so סוכות is always the third and last festival. If a person vowed after פסח, the סוכות that comes next is not his deadline. He can wait until the following year's סוכות, so he is not forced to bring his תודה on this סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: In their order: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
Yes
No

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: any three רגלים count. רבי שמעון: only in order, so סוכות is always the last one.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a person may bring offerings on חול המועד. The argument is only about when the בל תאחר deadline hits.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
in their order, yes (he is liable);
not in their order, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side to the תנא קמא in step 14, completing אביי's answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון counts the festivals only in order, so a person who vowed after פסח is not forced to bring his offering on the coming סוכות. He may wait until the next סוכות.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows a תודה on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next opinion in the ברייתא: a person may bring his תודה on חג הסוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: a person may bring his תודה on the festival of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא. This sets up the question of what exactly he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new opinion, from רבי שמעון's son. The wording 'on חג הסוכות' is unclear: does it mean the חול המועד days or the יום טוב itself? The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון
A thanks-offering, brought with loaves including חמץ
The festival of סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
A person may bring his thanks-offering on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה may be brought on חג הסוכות.

steps.title: When on סוכות does he mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון means חול המועד. If so, he would just be repeating the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If you say on חול המועד, that is the same as the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what time on סוכות he is talking about. It shows that 'חול המועד' cannot be the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already allowed a תודה on חול המועד of סוכות (step 10). A new named opinion should add something new. So reading him as meaning חול המועד makes his statement pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)
The intermediate days of the festival
That is the same as

phrases.english: When?
If you say on the intermediate days of the festival,
that is the same as the first tanna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what step 16 means, and rules out the first possible reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which days of סוכות רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is referring to.

steps.title: He means the יום טוב itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון must mean the actual יום טוב, because he holds that נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means on יום טוב itself, and he holds that vow-offerings and gift-offerings may be brought on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: he is talking about the יום טוב day of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון a real new position. Unlike the earlier view that forbade a תודה on the יום טוב of שבועות, he holds that voluntary offerings may be brought even on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
He holds
Vow-offerings and gift-offerings (voluntary offerings)
Are offered

phrases.english: Rather, on the Festival day itself,
and he holds that vow-offerings and gift-offerings
may be sacrificed on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He means יום טוב itself, and he allows נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון a separate voice in the larger argument about whether voluntary offerings may be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why mention סוכות specifically?
steps.stepSummary: If he allows voluntary offerings on any יום טוב, why did he name סוכות in particular?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about סוכות that he mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about why סוכות was named. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every יום טוב allows נדרים ונדבות, naming one festival seems unnecessary. A תודה cannot come on פסח because of its חמץ loaves, but שבועות would still work. So why not say 'on any יום טוב'?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
He mentioned / took as his example

phrases.english: And what is different about the festival of Sukkot that he cited it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 18's reading by questioning the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון named סוכות specifically.

steps.title: He follows his own view in a ברייתא where he argues with his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his own view about בל תאחר. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי שמעון first learns from the extra words 'חג הסוכות' that סוכות must be the last of the three רגלים. The son's different reading comes in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his own reasoning. As the ברייתא teaches, רבי שמעון says: the פסוק did not need to say 'חג הסוכות', since it was already speaking about it. Why was it said? To teach that this one is the last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he named סוכות because of his own view about בל תאחר. To show that view, it quotes a ברייתא that first gives his father רבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק. The son's different reading follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns from the extra mention of 'חג הסוכות' that the three רגלים must pass in order, ending with סוכות. This is only the first half of the ברייתא. His son reads the same extra words differently (next step), and that reading explains why he named סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Why was it said? (points to an extra word in a פסוק)
Last

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון reads the extra 'חג הסוכות' as 'this one is last': the three רגלים count only in order. His son reads the same words differently, as the next step shows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, follows his own line of reasoning,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
The verse need not have said 'the festival of Sukkot',
since the verse was already speaking about it.
Why, then, was it stated?
To say that this one is the last.
phrases.notes: סוכות must be the final festival of the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 19 by citing the ברייתא with the father's and son's competing readings. The son's reading, in step 21, completes the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוכות is named because of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's own view on בל תאחר, recorded in a ברייתא where he argues with his father. He holds that סוכות is the festival that triggers the deadline (step 21).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי שמעון learns from the extra words 'חג הסוכות' that סוכות is last.

steps.title: סוכות Is the Festival That Triggers the Deadline
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון explains that the פסוק names סוכות to teach that סוכות is the festival that causes a person to be late.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the פסוק names סוכות to teach that this festival is what causes the lateness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source that explains why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון singled out סוכות. סוכות is the festival that sets the deadline for בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike his father, who counts three festivals in order, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that סוכות itself sets the deadline. Every vow made during the year must be fulfilled by the end of סוכות, even a vow made just before it. That is why he named סוכות in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: causes / triggers (here, the transgression of בל תאחר)
the prohibition against delaying the fulfillment of a vow
to teach / to say (introducing what a פסוק comes to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: סוכות is the deadline festival for בל תאחר. That is why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון named it when he spoke about bringing a תודה on the actual יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
to say that this one (Sukkot) causes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה גּוֹרֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 20 by stating the actual derivation: סוכות is the trigger for בל תאחר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכות is the festival that causes a person to violate בל תאחר, so it is the final deadline for vowed offerings.

steps.title: The תודה Counts for שמחה but Not for חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a person who brings his תודה on the חג fulfills the מצוה of שמחה with it, but not the obligation of חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fulfills with it the מצוה of rejoicing, but he does not fulfill with it the obligation of the festival offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its next line. The תודה brought on the חג can count as the person's שמחה, but it cannot count as his חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate festival obligations: שלמי שמחה (eating meat to rejoice) and קרבן חגיגה. The ברייתא says the תודה works for the first but not for the second. The next step will ask why the second half even needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of rejoicing on the festival, fulfilled by eating שלמים meat
the obligatory festival peace-offering
fulfills (an obligation)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse שמחה with חגיגה. They are two different festival obligations, and the ברייתא treats them differently.

phrases.english: And he fulfills with it the obligation of rejoicing,
but he does not fulfill with it the obligation of the Festival offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹצֵא בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה, וְאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם חֲגִיגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 16 and quotes its next clause, opening a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה brought on the festival counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה.

steps.title: Isn't It Obvious? An Obligation Must Come from חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: obviously the תודה cannot count as חגיגה. חגיגה is an obligation, and any obligatory offering must come only from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! חגיגה is an obligation, and anything obligatory may only come from non-sacred animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for stating something that seems obvious. Why did it need to say that the תודה does not count as חגיגה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that an obligatory offering must be brought from an animal that is not already sacred. The תודה animal was already made holy because of the person's vow, so it obviously cannot be used for the obligatory חגיגה. So the ברייתא seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)
an obligatory matter / mandatory offering
non-sacred property

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that obligatory offerings come only from חולין is a basic principle of קדשים. Here it is used to question why the ברייתא needed to say anything.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
It (the Festival offering) is an obligatory matter,
and anything that is an obligatory matter
comes only from non-sacred property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second half of the ברייתא quoted in step 22 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תודה does not count as חגיגה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is already known that obligatory offerings must come from חולין, and the תודה is already sacred, so the statement teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Even If He Stipulated It in Advance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is needed for a case where the person stated at the time of his vow that the תודה should also count as his חגיגה. Even then, it does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed: even though he specified it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The ברייתא is teaching that the תודה does not count as חגיגה even if the person specifically stipulated that it should.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that a stipulation made at the time of the vow would work. The person never fully made the animal holy as a plain תודה, but only as a תודה that would also serve as his חגיגה. The ברייתא teaches that even so, he does not fulfill חגיגה with it.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not needed (except for this case); the statement is needed for a specific case
even though
he specified / stated explicitly

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for a case where he specified it explicitly.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּפָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 23 by identifying a case where the ruling is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he explicitly stipulated at the time of the vow that the תודה should also count as חגיגה, the stipulation might work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with an explicit stipulation, the תודה does not count as חגיגה.

steps.title: A Parallel Question from ריש לקיש to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares this to a question ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן about someone who vows a תודה and says he will also fulfill חגיגה with it, or who says 'I am a נזיר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי שמעון בן לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: one who says, 'It is upon me to bring a תודה, and I will fulfill with it my חגיגה obligation,' or 'I am a נזיר'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It starts to quote a question that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן about this same kind of stipulation, and the question continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's case matches the one we just described: a person who vows a תודה on condition that it also counts as his חגיגה. The mention of 'I am a נזיר' starts a second, parallel case. Its details and the answer come in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: as he asked of him
it is upon me (the formula for a vow, נדר)
thanks-offering
a nazirite

phrases.english: As he asked of him,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
One who says: It is upon me to bring a thanks-offering,
and I will fulfill with it my Festival-offering obligation;
or: I am a nazirite

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the case from step 24 (an explicit stipulation) to a known question from ריש לקיש to רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vow made on condition that the offering also fulfills another obligation (חגיגה, or נזירות) is valid, and what happens with it. The full question continues on the next עמוד.
